meta.title: California's Money, Past and Future
meta.unit_note: All money values are $ billions, nominal (not inflation- or population-adjusted), unless a field says otherwise.
meta.fiscal_year_label: FY 2026-27 means the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. California fiscal year = July 1-June 30.
meta.projection_end_note: Horizon set by maturity, not rounding: sold GO bonds end FY2056-57, sold lease-revenue bonds end FY2050-51, Treasurer intended-sales debt service ends FY2057-58. Years after a series ends are 0 for that series (or null where the series was never verified).
meta.generated_from: The sources listed in meta.sources; the chart and table read this file only.
meta.core_rule: Debt service is the outflow. Principal is a memo. Bond proceeds are not revenue.
meta.core_rule_detail: Debt service (principal + interest) sits INSIDE General Fund expenditure; it is never added on top of expenditure. Principal repaid is a memo and is also the decline in outstanding debt; never add principal outstanding to total debt service. Bond proceeds are never added to the General Fund revenue line. GO proceeds go to a bond fund for capital purposes, not to the GF operating budget.
meta.bases_warning: NEVER silently sum across different bases. General Fund core series, all-funds totals, bonded debt (a stock), and unfunded pension/OPEB liabilities (actuarial, different basis) are kept as separate, labelled series. Actuarial liabilities are NOT bonded debt. A mixed-basis context sum is given only in long_term_obligations_context with its basis warning attached, and it must not be charted as bonded debt.
meta.baseline_default: years[].baseline points at the DOF-based construction (baseline_dof). The LAO outlook baseline (baseline_lao) is a second, separately labelled series wherever it exists; it is NOT averaged with the DOF baseline and NOT used for scenario math.
meta.scenario_math: scenario_revenue(year) = baseline_revenue(year) + sum of checked props' revenue_delta(year); scenario_expenditure(year) = baseline_expenditure(year) + sum of checked props' debt_service_delta(year) + sum of checked props' program_spending_delta(year). Bond proceeds (bond_proceeds_memo, revenue_bonds_issued_memo) are NEVER added to revenue. Props with modelled=false contribute nothing and must render as notes, never as zero lines implying a measured zero effect. EXCEPTION - Prop 40: its revenue_delta is 2026 Billionaire Tax Reserve Fund revenue, NOT General Fund revenue. Never add it to baseline General Fund revenue and never add its Reserve Fund spending memo to General Fund expenditure; plot it as a separate Reserve Fund series. Its general_fund_revenue_delta and program_spending_delta are 0 in every row.
meta.prop_40_41_42_conflict: LAO warning: if Prop 41 or Prop 42 receives more yes votes than Prop 40, Prop 40 could be stopped from becoming law even if it gets yes votes from a majority of voters. The page must warn whenever Prop 40 is checked together with Prop 41 or Prop 42; do not sum them naively.

assumptions.baseline_dof_construction: ILLUSTRATION ONLY, NOT A FORECAST. Baseline revenue and non-debt expenditure are held at FY2026-27 levels in nominal dollars, EXCEPT baseline revenue falls from FY2031-32 onward by the Prop 30/55 midpoint $10B/yr (range $5-15B) because those rates expire at end-2030 under current law. Baseline expenditure in projection years = non-debt base ($242.798B = FY2026-27 expenditure $251.477B minus FY2026-27 gross debt service $8.679B) + DAR baseline debt service (sold + intended sales) that year. Baseline balance = baseline revenue - baseline expenditure. LAO and the Governor disagree by tens of billions even for 2026-27, so any single long baseline is illustrative by construction.
assumptions.baseline_lao_construction: LAO Nov 2025 Fiscal Outlook, current-law baseline, NOT a prediction. Balance/deficit values only, FY2026-27 through FY2029-30; null beyond its horizon. 2026-27 is a 'budget problem', not a Chart A operating balance. No revenue/expenditure split is encoded for the LAO series.
assumptions.bond_sale_timing_props_1_38: APPROVED EVEN-SPREAD ASSUMPTION: bonds sold evenly over the first 5 years after passage (FY2027-28-FY2031-32); each tranche repaid as level annual payments over the LAO term (Prop 1: 25 yrs, Prop 38: 20 yrs), first payment the fiscal year after sale. LAO gives no sale calendar for either prop.
assumptions.bond_interest_rate_props_1_38: No LAO rate is used. Implied rates are DERIVED (see each prop): solved so the level payment equals the LAO midpoint $550M/yr once all tranches are paying. Early ramp years are below $550M/yr.
assumptions.prop_98_bsa_passthrough: NOT separately modelled. Prop deltas are gross; new GF revenue could trigger a Prop 98 education share and a BSA deposit, so the discretionary GF effect could be smaller than the gross delta. Stated here, not hidden in a haircut.
assumptions.bond_funded_capital_spending: NOT shown as GF expenditure. Only debt service is the GF effect in Panel A; bond-funded capital spending is described in prop detail, never stacked with debt service for the same dollar.
assumptions.commercial_paper: GO commercial paper $1.346B outstanding (June 30, 2026) is EXCLUDED from the long-term schedule; it is routinely retired with long-term proceeds, and counting both would double-count. Footnote only.
assumptions.self_liquidating_go: Excluded from GF-supported series (outstanding $0.964B, lifetime debt service $1.519B, final year FY2055-56). Footnote only.
assumptions.refundings: Assumed none in the baseline. DAR already reflects refundings through June 30, 2026; future refundings replace old bonds and do not add principal.
assumptions.variable_rate_interest: DAR variable-rate interest is estimated at June 30, 2026 rates (2.10-2.70%), not fixed. Small: $0.434B lifetime vs $36.713B fixed GO interest.
assumptions.build_america_bonds_subsidy: DAR fixed-rate interest does not reflect the Build America Bonds federal subsidy (not pledged to debt service). Gross debt service is plotted; net-of-subsidy figures are footnoted where known (2025-26 net $6.42B vs gross $8.14B).

gaps: All-funds REVENUE annual series: not verified to a primary source, so all_funds revenue is null for every year. All-funds expenditure is verified only for FY2024-25, FY2025-26, FY2026-27 (LAO Spending Plan); null elsewhere. Do not backfill.

General Fund debt-service annual series for history years before FY2025-26: not verified (only DAR 2025-26 gross $8.14B and 2026-27 $8.679B are in the file). expenditure_existing_debt_service is null for earlier years; do not infer it from secondary summaries.

BSA (Budget Stabilization Account) annual series: no single-vintage complete series was verified. BSA anchors only, in reserves_anchors, with vintage per point. Never add a BSA figure from one vintage to a Chart A SFEU figure from another vintage.
General-purpose reserves (BSA + SFEU) per year: null in years[] for the vintage reason above; LAO-vintage combined anchors are in reserves_anchors only.
GO outstanding / debt-service annual series for history years before June 30, 2025: not verified; would require pulling each year's DAR snapshot one by one.
Final FY2025-26 actuals: not in July 2026 Chart A; FY2025-26 is enacted/estimate and FY2024-25 is revised. A future Chart A vintage will move these rows.

Remaining unissued bonds beyond the Treasurer's 2-year intended-sales plan (~$25.55B = $42.461B minus $16.911B): memo only, NO dated series. No official sale dates or rates exist; assigning a sale year would invent a schedule.
Prop 1 / Prop 38 sale calendars and nominal total debt service: not in LAO. Sale timing is the stated even-spread assumption; totals are derived arithmetic, labelled as such.
Prop 37 repayment schedule and borrower-repayment inflows: not in LAO. Memo issuance schedule is an assumption; repayments are note only.

Unfunded liabilities: only the anchors in long_term_obligations_context are verified. No annual unfunded-liability series is encoded (null by design). CalPERS state-share figures for June 30, 2025 and OPEB for June 30, 2025 were not verified in this pass; the June 30, 2025 OPEB valuation report exists but its headline total was not extracted, so it is not used.

LAO baseline beyond FY2029-30: null by design. Do not extend the LAO series to 2057 by invention; the DOF construction is the only baseline that runs to 2057-58, and it is labelled illustration, not forecast.

Unissued-bond discrepancy in the research memo (DAR total GO unissued $39.14B vs Appendix A sum $38.200B, ~$1.35B, consistent with commercial-paper treatment but not confirmed to a line item): this file uses the memo's clean GF figure $42.461B total GF-supported unissued ($37.794B GO non-self-liquidating + $4.667B LRB) and flags the discrepancy here rather than resolving it silently. DAR cover-letter 'over $44B' counts GO commercial paper and self-liquidating bonds and is not used as the GF figure.

FY2026-27 kind is Governor's Jan 2026 proposal per the task brief (Chart A July 2026 vintage). The enacted 2026-27 budget package totals (LAO Spending Plan: GF revenue $226.754B, GF expenditure $251.477B) happen to match the Chart A row, but the row is still labelled proposal, not enacted actual, in this file.

Prop 40 unverified items (see prop-40.unverified): Dec 31, 2026 valuations; FTB residency rulings for named departures; whether courts uphold the Jan 1, 2026 date; control-weighted valuation; missing-billionaire count; lump/instalment mix. The $30B/$65B/$100B band is therefore conditional, with LOW confidence on any point estimate.

unissued_bonds_memo.remaining_note: Remaining = 42.461 - 16.911 = 25.55 (rounded). Memo only, no dated series. Largest unissued balances (DAR App A): Prop 4 (2024) $9.670B, Prop 2 (2024) K-12 $7.150B, Prop 1 (Mar 2024) behavioral health $5.158B, stem cell (2020) $4.028B.
unissued_bonds_memo.is_not_debt: Authorized but unissued bonds are NOT debt owed. Never add them to outstanding debt or to debt service until sold.

long_term_obligations_context.basis_warning: Bonded debt is a contractual stock with a fixed amortization schedule. Unfunded pension/OPEB liabilities are actuarial present values that move with returns, payroll, and assumptions and are paid through actuarially determined contributions, not a bond schedule. They are measured on different bases and must never be charted as one undifferentiated 'debt' series. Any sum across them is a context figure only, labelled with its basis and date.

propositions.summary: One-time 5% tax on net worth of billionaires resident Jan 1, 2026; real estate, pensions, retirement accounts generally excluded. Revenue goes to the 2026 Billionaire Tax Reserve Fund (90% health, 10% education/food assistance), expressly exempt from Prop 98, Prop 2, and Gann rules - it is NOT General Fund money.
propositions.lao: LAO (Official Voter Information Guide, verbatim substance): the state 'probably would collect tens of billions of dollars' spread over several years; 'exactly when and how much the state would collect is very hard to predict'; possible ongoing income-tax decrease of 'less than $1 billion per year'; administration 'tens of millions of dollars per year for several years'. LAO gives NO point estimate; the band below is the independent triangulation, not the LAO.
propositions.note: PLOT AS A BAND ($30-100B) WITH A $65B CENTRAL LINE, never as a single number. Central $65B is a SYNTHESIS, not a published estimate (see central_line_label_exact). Revenue is NOT spending and Prop 40 revenue is NOT General Fund money: it is exempt from Prop 98 / Prop 2 / Gann rules, goes to the 2026 Billionaire Tax Reserve Fund, 90% health / 10% education-food, appropriation caps $22.5B + $2.5B = $25B/yr. The cap does not bind on the $13B/yr central instalment path but would bind on a $65B lump sum in 2027, stretching spending past 2031. General Fund program_spending_delta is therefore 0 and Reserve Fund spending is a separate memo series only. FTB administration costs (LAO: tens of millions/yr for several years, paid from the new revenues) are small relative to these totals and are NOT deducted in the table; note them, do not net them silently. Blue Sky Consulting Group's headline and sensitivity top are NOT used as central or high (cross-check only: the headline applies no avoidance haircut). LAO warning: if Prop 41 or Prop 42 receives more yes votes than Prop 40, Prop 40 could be stopped from becoming law even if it gets yes votes from a majority of voters. The page must warn whenever Prop 40 is checked together with Prop 41 or Prop 42; do not sum them naively.
propositions.conflict_with_prop_41_42: LAO warning: if Prop 41 or Prop 42 receives more yes votes than Prop 40, Prop 40 could be stopped from becoming law even if it gets yes votes from a majority of voters. The page must warn whenever Prop 40 is checked together with Prop 41 or Prop 42; do not sum them naively.

propositions.central_line_label_exact: Central $65B - SYNTHESIS, not a published estimate: midpoint of Jaros & Rauh's face-value range after observed departures ($59-72B); before litigation discount; excludes missing billionaires and control-weighting. Low $30B is their litigation-weighted (50% survival) estimate; high $100B is the Galle/Boll benchmark.
propositions.confidence: LOW on any point estimate; MEDIUM that pre-litigation face value after observed departures is ~$59-72B.

one_time_total_sources.low: Jaros & Rauh, NBER WP 35899 (Oct 2026), litigation-weighted expected value; their published range is $28-36B. NOTE: this is face value x a 0.50 litigation-survival weight (a FASB 'more likely than not' accounting convention), NOT a court forecast. If the law survives intact (weight 1.0), their own estimate is $59-72B, not $30B.
one_time_total_sources.central: SYNTHESIS, not a published estimate - label it exactly as such on every use. Midpoint of Jaros & Rauh's two face-value endpoints after publicly observed departures: $71.17B (Zuckerberg stays) and $59.15B (Zuckerberg excluded) = $65.16B, rounded to $65B. No litigation discount, no extra blanket avoidance haircut on top of departures (that would double-count the main avoidance channel), $0 for missing billionaires, $0 for control-weighting.
one_time_total_sources.high: Galle et al. / Boll, Saez & Zucman benchmark ($98-104B, rounded to $100B). Requires the Jan 1, 2026 residency date to hold for essentially everyone and only ~10% total erosion.

propositions.annual_deltas_coverage: Five instalment years ONLY. No revenue delta in any other year; annual_deltas contains exactly those five rows. Do not plot a single number without the band.
propositions.fiscal_year_mapping: EXPLICIT MAPPING (do not silently shift calendar to fiscal years): the triangulation memo's instalment years are CALENDAR 2027-2031 (tax due with 2026 returns in 2027, five equal instalments). This JSON maps calendar instalment year Y to the fiscal-year label ending June 30 of the SAME calendar year - 2027->2026-27, 2028->2027-28, 2029->2028-29, 2030->2029-30, 2031->2030-31 - because returns are filed in spring of the instalment year, inside that fiscal year. STRADDLE NOTE: the first instalment therefore falls in the FY2026-27 Governor's-proposal baseline year, not in the first full post-passage fiscal year (2027-28); the other four fall in projection years. If the FTB instead sets instalment due dates after June 30, each instalment shifts one fiscal year later; the five annual amounts ($6.0B low / $13.0B central / $20.0B high) and the $30B / $65B / $100B totals do not change.

deferral_upside_footnote_only.note: FOOTNOTE ONLY, NEVER baked into the central total. If ALL taxpayers elect instalments, total cash rises 15% (effective rate 5.00% -> 5.75%) on the central path. The lump/instalment mix is unknown, so chart the base-tax table and footnote this path.

ongoing_drag_memo.note: SEPARATE MEMO LINE, NEVER netted into the one-time total and NEVER shown as a subtraction from the one-time bar. Income-tax drag only, if departures are permanent.

income_tax_drag_range_per_year.basis: LAO low end (<$1B/yr, shown as $0.5B floor for charting the range) to Jaros & Rauh high end ($3.5B/yr). LAO and Rauh differ on scope and on whether a mass permanent exodus is modelled; both are income-tax only.

ongoing_drag_memo.walczak_all_taxes_footnote: Walczak (California Tax Foundation): $3.53-4.49B/yr in ALL state taxes including sales and spillover effects ($2.77B/yr for the nine publicly identified emigres alone). BROADER SCOPE than the income-tax range above; do NOT compare it directly to the LAO income-tax figure and do NOT add it to the income-tax range.

undiscounted_break_even_on_65B.note: Undiscounted only. Discounted, and if departures are temporary or replaced, break-even stretches; if permanent and growing, it shortens.

ongoing_drag_memo.excluded_from_cash_flows: Rauh's net-present-value figure (a present value over an infinite horizon under stated departure-fraction and discount assumptions, highly sensitive to both) is EXCLUDED from every cash-flow year and from every annual row in this file. Do not present it as a cash loss in any year.

unverified: Dec 31, 2026 valuations (the actual tax base date, after the triangulation memo's retrieval date). Tech wealth moved violently during 2026, so the final base could be tens of billions above or below any mid-year snapshot.

FTB residency rulings for named departures (Page, Brin, Thiel, Hankey, Spielberg, Kalanick, Sacks, Zuckerberg) and any stealth departures with no press/property trail. A public move announcement is not a tax-residency determination; the FTB uses a totality test.
Whether courts uphold the Jan 1, 2026 residency date, or reform it to Election Day (which would let all nine identified departures escape).
Whether the control-weighted valuation applies to publicly traded dual-class stock, and in what aggregate amount (unquantified; excluded from central and high).
Missing-billionaire count and wealth (Forbes under-coverage estimates imply $6.7B to $24.6B of tax, or $0 collectible on Rauh's standard; central uses $0).
Lump-sum vs instalment mix, and therefore actual deferral-charge revenue.
Whether Prop 41/42 outpoll Prop 40 (in which case the Prop 40 scenario is $0; the conflict warning must remain).
Federal matching on Prop 40-funded Medi-Cal spending (upside to spending power, not to state revenue; never added to the revenue bar).
